Explanation: INFO has arity -1, so a bare `INFO` leaves section NULL, and it is passed to strcasecmp() before the NULL case is handled: the server crashes.

expire_at is read only when o.flags has one of SET_EX|SET_PX|SET_EXAT|SET_PXAT, and in exactly that case set_opts_has_expiry() (cmdutil.c) returned nonzero and expire_at was assigned. Proof needs set_opts_has_expiry's definition.
store_lookup() returns NULL for a missing key, and e->v.str.len is read before the e == NULL check: GETRANGE on a missing key crashes.
Same NULL dereference as line 865 (e->v.str.ptr); it goes away when line 865 is fixed by checking e before use.

An unterminated quoted value frees val and then jumps to `fail`, which frees it again (double free).
The 'line too long' error path returns without fclose(fp).
The new bucket array is allocated before the rehash-in-progress check, and that check returns -1 without freeing it. Reachable via ht_maybe_resize().
Same leak as the Clang alert on this line.

The check is off by one (> instead of >=): level == LOG_NLEVELS reads past level_names[]. Reachable: config accepts a numeric loglevel with the same off-by-one, and CONFIG GET loglevel calls log_level_name().
When bind() fails the function returns without closing the socket.
Clang's path comes through net_accept(): accept() fills in the sockaddr_storage before sa_family is read, but Clang's model of accept() doesn't record the write.
memcpy copies sizeof(SNAP_MAGIC) == 9 bytes (including the NUL) into char magic[8]: a 1-byte out-of-bounds write into the next field (masked only because version is assigned afterwards).
If write_header() fails, the function returns without fclose(w.fp).
On a short fread() the function returns -1 without freeing buf.
read_u8() returns 0 only after fread() filled in `type`; Clang doesn't model fread() as writing the buffer.
validate_list() already walked the same payload with an identical cursor and checked every cur_blob(), so cur_blob() cannot fail here and p is always set.
The loop stops when fread() returns 0 and ferror() is checked after the loop; calling fread() after a failed read is not undefined behavior and has no harmful effect here.
One extra fread() at EOF just returns 0 and ends the loop; harmless.
When parse_len() fails, the error branch sets the message but doesn't return, so the uninitialized length n is compared on the next line.
If the trailing CRLF is missing, the function returns PARSE_ERROR without freeing arg. A client can leak memory with malformed requests.

Clang assumes clients_remove() may fail to find a client that is in the array. Every client with fd >= 0 is in the array (client_create adds it), and client_free removes exactly those, so no freed client stays in the array.
After client_free(srv, c) the log message reads c->id: use after free on every client disconnect.
Returns a pointer to a local array; server_info() uses it after the function returns.
Same dangling pointer as the Clang alert on this line.
With an empty keyspace and a verbose INFO section, used_bytes / nkeys divides by zero.
Clang assumes nclients + 1 can wrap to 0 so that the array is never allocated; nclients is bounded by max_clients.
Same infeasible assumption as server.c:127: client_free() always removes a client that is in the array, so the loop never sees a freed client.

ht_count() > 0 was checked and n >= 1, and ht_random_entry() (hashtable.c) never returns NULL for a nonempty table (it probes only buckets that can hold entries, even mid-rehash), so victim is set. Proof needs ht_random_entry's definition.
store_remove_entry() frees victim, and then victim->key and victim->keylen are passed to on_remove: use after free whenever eviction runs with AOF enabled.
A zero-length value uses the static empty_value buffer; on the out-of-memory path the copy is released with free() instead of free_value(), freeing a non-heap pointer.
